newsitem.title: USA: Goldman Sachs posts record first-half profit.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs posts record first-half profit.

text.p: Goldman Sachs & Co. said Wednesday that earnings fell in its latest quarter, hurt partly by a slowdown in initial public offerings.
The closely held investment bank said pretax earnings fell to $610 million in its second quarter from $905 million in the first quarter and $709 million in the 1996 second quarter.
Another Wall Street firm, A.G. Edwards Inc., said Tuesday that earnings fell 3 percent in the latest quarter.

Though A.G. Edwards, mainly a retail broker, and Goldman are in different lines of business, analysts said the reports illustrate that profits at Wall Street firms are likely to slump in the latest quarter.

Raphael Soifer at Brown Brothers Harriman said the markets affect different firms in different ways. Goldman Sachs is a big player in initial public stock offerings, for example, and the quarter was sluggish for that business. The bond market was weak in March and early April, he added.
A source familiar with the results cautioned against reading too much into the drop from the first quarter, when earnings were very strong. Second-quarter results were respectable, the source added.
Goldman noted that first-half earnings of $1.52 billion set a record and were up 19 percent from a year earlier.
The firm said in a statement that revenues rose to $3.6 billion in the first half from $3.1 billion a year ago. Expenses climbed to $2.12 billion from $1.86 billion.

Soifer said he expects other big firms, including Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co. and Lehman Bros Holdings Inc., to post lower earnings for the latest quarter compared to the prior quarter. Both firms are expected to report earnings next week.
Dean Eberling at Smith Barney said he expects Wall Street firms in general to have lower earnings when the April-through-June quarter is compared to the January-through-March quarter.
Employment at Goldman rose to about 9,500 worldwide, up from about 9,000 at the end of the first quarter.
A.G. Edwards said Tuesday that net income fell to $54.5 million, or 83 cents a share, in its first quarter ended May 31, from $56.4 million, or 87 cents a share, a year earlier.
